claim: Longer common prefixes between paired preference sequences exacerbate gradient cancellation, leading to more severe optimization issues.
falsifier: Train models with paired data having varying common prefix lengths (e.g., 10%, 30%, 50% of total length) and measure gradient norms for prefix tokens; the claim predicts that longer prefixes yield smaller gradients.

conditions: paired sequences constructed from tree search (leading to longer common prefixes)
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported analysis comparing DPO and FPO; transfer beyond these settings is unestablished.

title: Length of the common–severity of gradient cancellation mechanism

claim: Incorporating uncertainty as auxiliary information during fine-tuning improves the evaluation performance of LLM evaluators, particularly in out-of-distribution scenarios.
falsifier: Test whether fine-tuning LLM evaluators with an additional uncertainty prediction task improves their accuracy on held-out OOD evaluation sets.

conditions: fine-tuning with uncertainty as auxiliary information
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported OOD test set with 220 instances and the specific fine-tuning procedure; transfer beyond them is unestablished.

title: Incorporating uncertainty as auxiliary for evaluation performance
